objects.description: Sentinel empty type used primarily as a placeholder error type (e.g., when mapping an error to void/monostate). It has no data or behavior.
Tag type to request in-place construction of the value inside tl::expected. The constant tl::in_place is the canonical instance.
Tag type used to construct tl::expected in the error state in-place (with an error value). The constant tl::unexpect is the canonical instance.
Internal tag type used to select constructors that do not initialize the union storage within expected internals.
Internal tag to enable constructing expected’s base classes while conditionally deleting default constructors.

functions.name: tl::unexpected::value
functions.signature: constexpr const E& tl::unexpected<E>::value() const &
functions.description: Returns a const lvalue reference to the stored unexpected error value. Use to read the contained error without moving it.
requirements: This member is available on tl::unexpected<E> where E is not void.
Object must be initialized (tl::unexpected has deleted default ctor; value() just returns member).

functions.name: tl::make_unexpected
functions.signature: template <class E> tl::unexpected<typename std::decay<E>::type> tl::make_unexpected(E&& e)
functions.description: Factory function to create an unexpected<E> from a value, forwarding and decaying the argument. Use to construct unexpected without explicitly naming the template parameter.
requirements: E must be decayed-constructible into unexpected<decay<E>>::value_type.
Argument e is forwarded; avoid passing dangling references.

functions.name: tl::operator==
functions.signature: template <class E> constexpr bool tl::operator==(const tl::unexpected<E>& lhs, const tl::unexpected<E>& rhs)
functions.description: Compares two unexpected<E> for equality by comparing their contained error values with operator==.
requirements: E must support equality comparison (operator==).

functions.name: tl::operator==
functions.signature: template <class T, class E, class U, class F> constexpr bool tl::operator==(const tl::expected<T,E>& lhs, const tl::expected<U,F>& rhs)
functions.description: Compares two expected values: if both hold values, compares *lhs == *rhs; if both hold errors, compares lhs.error() == rhs.error(); otherwise returns false.
requirements: Value types T and U must be equality-comparable when both present.
Error types E and F must be equality-comparable when both are errors.

functions.name: tl::operator!=
functions.signature: template <class E> constexpr bool tl::operator!=(const tl::unexpected<E>& lhs, const tl::unexpected<E>& rhs)
functions.description: Inequality comparison for two unexpected<E>, delegating to the contained error value’s operator!=.
requirements: E must support inequality comparison (operator!=).

functions.name: tl::operator!=
functions.signature: template <class T, class E, class U, class F> constexpr bool tl::operator!=(const tl::expected<T,E>& lhs, const tl::expected<U,F>& rhs)
functions.description: Inequality comparison mirroring operator== semantics for tl::expected.
requirements: Same comparability requirements as operator==.

functions.name: tl::operator<
functions.signature: template <class E> constexpr bool tl::operator<(const tl::unexpected<E>& lhs, const tl::unexpected<E>& rhs)
functions.description: Strict-weak-order comparison for unexpected<E> by comparing contained error values with operator<.
requirements: E must support operator<.

functions.name: tl::operator<=
functions.signature: template <class E> constexpr bool tl::operator<=(const tl::unexpected<E>& lhs, const tl::unexpected<E>& rhs)
functions.description: Less-or-equal comparison for unexpected<E> by comparing contained error values with operator<=.
requirements: E must support operator<=.

functions.name: tl::operator>
functions.signature: template <class E> constexpr bool tl::operator>(const tl::unexpected<E>& lhs, const tl::unexpected<E>& rhs)
functions.description: Greater-than comparison for unexpected<E> by comparing contained error values with operator>.
requirements: E must support operator>.

functions.name: tl::operator>=
functions.signature: template <class E> constexpr bool tl::operator>=(const tl::unexpected<E>& lhs, const tl::unexpected<E>& rhs)
functions.description: Greater-or-equal comparison for unexpected<E> by comparing contained error values with operator>=.
requirements: E must support operator>=.

functions.name: tl::expected::and_then
functions.signature: template <class F> TL_EXPECTED_11_CONSTEXPR auto tl::expected<T,E>::and_then(F&& f) & -> decltype(tl::detail::and_then_impl(std::declval<tl::expected<T,E>&>(), std::forward<F>(f)))
functions.description: Monadic bind: if this has a value, invokes f with the value and returns its result (which must be an expected-like); otherwise propagates the error.
requirements: This->has_value() determines behavior; no precondition to call.
F must be invocable with *this (or no args if T is void) and must return a tl::expected<…, E2>.
If T is not void, dereferencing value must be valid.

functions.name: tl::expected::map
functions.signature: template <class F> TL_EXPECTED_11_CONSTEXPR auto tl::expected<T,E>::map(F&& f) & -> decltype(tl::detail::expected_map_impl(std::declval<tl::expected<T,E>&>(), std::forward<F>(f)))
functions.description: Transforms the contained value with f if present, wrapping the result in expected; otherwise propagates error. Alias: transform.
requirements: F must be invocable with *this (or no args if T is void).
If f returns void, the result type is expected<void,E>. Otherwise expected<decay_t<R>,E>.

functions.name: tl::expected::transform
functions.signature: template <class F> TL_EXPECTED_11_CONSTEXPR auto tl::expected<T,E>::transform(F&& f) & -> decltype(tl::detail::expected_map_impl(std::declval<tl::expected<T,E>&>(), std::forward<F>(f)))
functions.description: Alias of map(): transforms the contained value if present; otherwise propagates error.
requirements: Same as map().

functions.name: tl::expected::map_error
functions.signature: template <class F> TL_EXPECTED_11_CONSTEXPR auto tl::expected<T,E>::map_error(F&& f) & -> decltype(tl::detail::map_error_impl(std::declval<tl::expected<T,E>&>(), std::forward<F>(f)))
functions.description: Transforms the error with f if no value is present; otherwise returns the value unchanged.
requirements: F must be invocable with error() and may return a new error type or void.
If F returns void, error type becomes tl::monostate.

functions.name: tl::expected::transform_error
functions.signature: template <class F> TL_EXPECTED_11_CONSTEXPR auto tl::expected<T,E>::transform_error(F&& f) & -> decltype(tl::detail::map_error_impl(std::declval<tl::expected<T,E>&>(), std::forward<F>(f)))
functions.description: Alias of map_error(): transforms the error if present.
requirements: Same as map_error().

functions.name: tl::expected::or_else
functions.signature: template <class F> tl::expected<T,E> TL_EXPECTED_11_CONSTEXPR tl::expected<T,E>::or_else(F&& f) &
functions.description: If no value is present, calls f(error()) for recovery, then returns this (or the result if f returns expected). If a value is present, returns this unchanged.
requirements: F must be invocable with error(); it may return an expected or void (see implementation notes).
Behavior depends on SFINAE: if F returns expected, that is returned on error; if void, this is returned after calling f.

functions.name: tl::expected::operator=
functions.signature: template <class U = T, class G = T, typename std::enable_if<std::is_nothrow_constructible<T, U&&>::value, int>::type* = nullptr, typename std::enable_if<!std::is_void<G>::value, int>::type* = nullptr, typename std::enable_if<(!std::is_same<tl::expected<T,E>, tl::detail::decay_t<U>>::value && !tl::detail::conjunction<std::is_scalar<T>, std::is_same<T, tl::detail::decay_t<U>>>::value && std::is_constructible<T, U>::value && std::is_assignable<G&, U>::value && std::is_nothrow_move_constructible<E>::value), int>::type* = nullptr> tl::expected<T,E>& tl::expected<T,E>::operator=(U&& v)
functions.description: Assigns a new value to the expected. If it already holds a value, assigns to it; otherwise destroys the error and constructs T in-place from v. This overload is selected when T is nothrow-constructible from U&&.
requirements: U must be constructible into T and assignable to T&.
E must be nothrow move constructible for the error-to-value transition path.
T must not be void.
Not selected if U decays to expected<T,E> or if U is the same scalar type as T (SFINAE).

functions.name: tl::expected::emplace
functions.signature: template <class... Args, typename std::enable_if<std::is_constructible<T, Args&&...>::value, int>::type* = nullptr> void tl::expected<T,E>::emplace(Args&&... args)
functions.description: Destroys the current state (value or error) and constructs a new value T in-place from the provided arguments. Provides strong exception-safety when needed per implementation variants.
requirements: T must be constructible from Args...
If currently holds a value, T’s destructor is called before reconstruction.
If currently holds an error, its destructor is called before constructing T.
If construction throws (when exceptions enabled), original error is restored in the throwing path (non-nothrow variant).

functions.name: tl::expected::swap
functions.signature: template <class OT = T, class OE = E> tl::detail::enable_if_t<tl::detail::is_swappable<OT>::value && tl::detail::is_swappable<OE>::value && (std::is_nothrow_move_constructible<OT>::value || std::is_nothrow_move_constructible<OE>::value)> tl::expected<T,E>::swap(tl::expected<T,E>& rhs) noexcept(std::is_nothrow_move_constructible<T>::value && tl::detail::is_nothrow_swappable<T>::value && std::is_nothrow_move_constructible<E>::value && tl::detail::is_nothrow_swappable<E>::value)
functions.description: Swaps this expected with rhs. If both have values, swaps values; if both have errors, swaps errors; if one has a value and the other an error, performs the appropriate move-construct/assignment to exchange states with strong exception safety where possible.
requirements: T and E must be swappable (ADL) and at least one of T or E must be nothrow move-constructible.
If one side holds a value and the other an error, T and E must be move-constructible as required by the chosen codepath.

functions.name: tl::expected::operator->
functions.signature: constexpr const T* tl::expected<T,E>::operator->() const
functions.description: Pointer-like access to the contained value (const). Asserts in debug builds if no value is present.
requirements: T must not be void.
this->has_value() must be true; otherwise TL_ASSERT triggers (undefined behavior in non-asserting builds).

functions.name: tl::expected::operator*
functions.signature: template <class U = T, typename tl::detail::enable_if_t<!std::is_void<U>::value>* = nullptr> constexpr const U& tl::expected<T,E>::operator*() const &
functions.description: Dereferences to a const lvalue reference of the contained value. Asserts if no value present.
requirements: T must not be void.
this->has_value() must be true; otherwise TL_ASSERT triggers.

functions.name: tl::expected::has_value
functions.signature: constexpr bool tl::expected<T,E>::has_value() const noexcept
functions.description: Returns true if the expected contains a value, false if it contains an error.

functions.name: tl::expected::operator bool
functions.signature: constexpr explicit tl::expected<T,E>::operator bool() const noexcept
functions.description: Boolean conversion that returns has_value(). Allows using expected in boolean contexts.

functions.name: tl::expected::value
functions.signature: template <class U = T, typename tl::detail::enable_if_t<!std::is_void<U>::value>* = nullptr> TL_EXPECTED_11_CONSTEXPR const U& tl::expected<T,E>::value() const &
functions.description: Returns the contained value as a const lvalue reference if present; otherwise throws tl::bad_expected_access<E> (or terminates if exceptions are disabled).
requirements: T must not be void.
If !has_value(), this throws bad_expected_access<E> via TL_EXPECTED_THROW_EXCEPTION (terminates when exceptions are disabled).

functions.name: tl::expected::error
functions.signature: constexpr const E& tl::expected<T,E>::error() const &
functions.description: Returns the contained error as a const lvalue reference. Asserts in debug builds if a value is present.
requirements: this->has_value() must be false; otherwise TL_ASSERT triggers.

functions.name: tl::expected::value_or
functions.signature: template <class U> constexpr T tl::expected<T,E>::value_or(U&& v) const &
functions.description: Returns the contained value if present, otherwise returns a copy of v converted to T. Requires T to be copy-constructible and convertible from U&&.
requirements: T must be copy-constructible.
U&& must be convertible to T.

functions.description: Returns a constant C-string describing the error: "Bad expected access".
requirements: None.

functions.name: tl::bad_expected_access::error
functions.signature: const E& tl::bad_expected_access<E>::error() const &
functions.description: Accesses the stored error payload as a const lvalue reference.
requirements: None.

functions.name: tl::swap
functions.signature: template <class T, class E, tl::detail::enable_if_t<(std::is_void<T>::value || std::is_move_constructible<T>::value) && tl::detail::is_swappable<T>::value && std::is_move_constructible<E>::value && tl::detail::is_swappable<E>::value>* = nullptr> void tl::swap(tl::expected<T,E>& lhs, tl::expected<T,E>& rhs) noexcept(noexcept(lhs.swap(rhs)))
functions.description: ADL-friendly free swap for tl::expected. Delegates to lhs.swap(rhs).
requirements: Same constraints as member swap: T and E must be swappable; T is void or move-constructible; E is move-constructible.
